The deposit's codebook.xlsx lists Variable / Label / Value for 146 variables and names each one exactly as the response table names its items apart from case, so each of the 8 items is tied to its text and to its own numbered value labels by a label match rather than an order inference. All 8 items resolve and all 39 shipped option cells re-derive from the workbook. validate_items.R reports item-set and resp-set matching live data. Administered language is Chinese (rural Zhejiang villages) and the deposit carries no Chinese item text -- codebook.xlsx holds 4 CJK characters, all in the font name SimSun, and raw.xlsx holds 0 -- so this is the translated_substitute fallback with language=Chinese, re-counted by rederive_coach.py at verification time. One shared 5-level run keyed 1 = Strongly agree to 5 = Strongly disagree, so higher resp means less satisfaction; q2 never reaches level 5 in the data, giving 39 option cells rather than 40. Scoring direction was checked against this table's own data rather than assumed, as #1831 asks. q3 and q8 are the two negatively worded items and carry the same ascending keys as the six positive ones, so they should invert; instead their mean r with the rest is +0.237 and +0.154, positive like every other item, and their item means of 2.57 and 2.28 fall inside the positive items' 2.21-2.59 range, where the printed labels would place a sample this satisfied near 4. Both signatures agree the stored values depart from the printed labels for those two items, so they ship with item text and no option label, 29 of 39 rows carrying option_text. The verify script recomputes both and fails if either signature reverses.
